title: std-doc — the doc that documents itself

root.summary: std-doc is the living-document standard: a single self-contained HTML page, served locally, that the reader can TALK TO. They select a sentence, pick an element, or leave a page note; the comment lands in a local inbox; the agent reads it, edits the page in place, and the page reloads and walks the reader through exactly what changed. No chat round-trip — the document IS the conversation. This doc is itself a std-doc: authored as a source.json doc-tree, derived to HTML by the tool's own publish.py. The tool documents itself.

facets.what: A living-document standard + a stdlib-only engine that makes any folder of HTML listen.
facets.dependencies: Python 3 standard library + a browser. Nothing else for the core. (Mermaid diagrams use a CDN in served mode; freezing diagrams needs the mermaid CLI.)
facets.license: MIT — self-contained in the skill directory.
facets.shape: Four moves: Method, Style, Serve, Respond. One optional Move 0 (data-derived docs) sits in front for structured, multi-page documents like this one.
facets.the test: Open it in a browser. That is the only honest check that it renders.

nodes.title: What is a Living Document
nodes.tagline: the document is the conversation

diagrams.caption: the loop — no chat round-trip
diagrams.ascii:
reader selects a sentence
        |
        v
  comment lands in feedback/inbox.jsonl  ──►  agent (Monitor fires)
        ^                                          |
        |                                          v
  page reloads, walks you            agent edits the HTML in place
  through what changed   ◄──  + appends a batch to history.json

sections.name: The core idea
sections.summary: A living document is the default shape for anything worth a reader's attention. It is one self-contained HTML page, served locally, that listens.

items.name: Talk to the page, not a chatbot
items.desc: The reader selects a sentence, picks an element, or leaves a page note. The comment is the unit of conversation, anchored to the exact text it is about.

items.name: The agent edits in place
items.desc: There is no separate reply thread. The agent changes the document itself, then the page reloads with scroll preserved and walks the reader to each change.

items.name: Self-contained + local
items.desc: One HTML page, served from localhost by a stdlib HTTP server. No build pipeline, no framework, no network dependency for the core.

sections.name: When to reach for it
sections.summary: Any time a reader should be able to respond to a document instead of replying in chat.

items.name: Proposals and designs
items.desc: Draft something the reader can comment on sentence-by-sentence — the open decisions sit waiting to be clicked.

items.name: Existing static HTML
items.desc: If you already have a folder of *.html and only want commenting, skip straight to Move 3 (Serve). The engine works on any folder of pages.

nodes.title: From Zero to a Listening Doc
nodes.tagline: one command, then open the localhost URL

diagrams.caption: setup.sh does inject + serve in one step
diagrams.ascii:
setup.sh <your-doc-dir> [port]
     |
     ├─ inject.py   → adds the feedback <link>/<script> to every *.html (idempotent)
     │                 + creates feedback/inbox.jsonl + feedback/history.json
     └─ server.py   → picks a free port (5050+), serves with --idle-timeout 0
                       prints  http://localhost:PORT   ◄── open THIS, not file://

sections.name: The one command
sections.summary: One script injects the widget and starts the server.

items.name: setup.sh
items.desc: Runs inject + serve, picks a free port (5050+), starts with --idle-timeout 0, and prints the URL.

citations.note: inject + serve in one step; named in SKILL.md

items.name: Open the http:// URL, not file://
items.desc: Only the served copy listens. A file:// page renders but shows no widget — the injected tags resolve /lib/* through the server.

sections.name: Then arm the watcher
sections.summary: Without a Monitor on the inbox you are collecting comments nobody reads. This is the step that closes the loop.

items.name: watch.py
items.desc: A persistent Monitor on watch.py does two jobs: it streams each new inbox line as a notification AND writes a presence heartbeat to feedback/watcher.json so the reader's page shows a calm '● watching' dot.

citations.note: inbox tail + presence heartbeat; named in SKILL.md

items.name: Don't poll in a loop
items.desc: Let the Monitor notification arrive. Polling burns context for nothing.

nodes.title: Move 1 — Method: Write by Descent
nodes.tagline: top-down by dependency, ending in cruxes

diagrams.caption: descent — start at what the reader looks at, ask what must be true below
diagrams.ascii:
[ the one line that matters ]   ← render it, in colour
        ↑ cannot exist without
  [ prerequisite layer ]          ← each property names a prereq
        ↑ cannot exist without
  [ prerequisite layer ]
        ↑ cannot exist without
  [ ground you already stand on ] ← light it green: HERE

  forward build order = this chain, reversed

sections.name: Top-down, not wish-list
sections.summary: Don't write bottom-up ('here's what we have, here's what we could add'). Start with the single artifact the reader will look at, then at every layer ask: for this to exist, what must be true the layer below?

items.name: The forcing function
items.desc: The endpoint conscripts every layer beneath it, so you never have to argue for the prerequisites — the top line visibly demands them. The proof of the proposal is the unwind itself.

items.name: Two honesty rules
items.desc: Separate net-new from reuse ruthlessly (trust comes from NOT rebuilding what exists), and name the one unglamorous gotcha out loud as its own layer.

sections.name: The seven beats
sections.summary: The skeleton has a block for each beat.

items.name: 1. The one-sentence ask
items.desc: Concrete, human, what-they-get — not 'a system'.

items.name: 2. The method box
items.desc: State that the endpoint is the forcing function.

items.name: 3. Layer 0 — render the endpoint
items.desc: Show the actual artifact in colour; list its hard properties (each secretly names a prerequisite).

items.name: 4. The descent
items.desc: The vertical stack, each layer joined by '↑ cannot … without'; tag every layer net-new or reuse; light the bottom green.

items.name: 5. The diagrams
items.desc: One per load-bearing idea (six idioms — see Move 2).

items.name: 6. Fold it forward
items.desc: The same chain as a build table, Phase 0…N; call out reuse vs the honest first brick.

items.name: 7. The cruxes
items.desc: End on the 1–3 decisions genuinely the reader's to make; mark them '◀ YOUR CALL'; commit your own lean first, then invite override.

nodes.title: Move 3 — Serve: Make the Page Listen
nodes.tagline: inject · server · watch — the stdlib seam

diagrams.caption: the three engine parts
diagrams.ascii:
inject.py  → adds <link>/<script> to every *.html (idempotent)
               creates feedback/inbox.jsonl + feedback/history.json
  server.py  → tiny stdlib HTTP server: serves pages, accepts the POST, exposes /info
  feedback.js/css → floating 💬, select-to-comment, polls history.json, auto-reloads
  watch.py   → tails the inbox (notifications) + writes watcher.json heartbeat

sections.name: Three parts, all stdlib
sections.summary: The engine in engine/ depends on nothing but Python's standard library.

items.name: inject.py
items.desc: Adds the feedback link/script pair to every *.html (idempotent) and creates the feedback files. Re-run after any full HTML rewrite — a from-scratch regeneration silently strips the injected tags.

items.name: server.py
items.desc: A tiny dev server: serves pages, accepts the comment POST, exposes /info and routes /lib/* to the skill's engine/lib/.

items.name: feedback.js / feedback.css
items.desc: The browser client: floating 💬, select-to-comment, structured controls, presence, threaded history. Polls history.json and auto-reloads on a new batch.

citations.note: the client; ~1,272 LOC of the engine

sections.name: Structured controls
sections.summary: When the answer is really 'which of these?', embed a radio / checkbox / select. The reader answers by picking; the selection lands as a structured control comment with no prose to parse.

items.name: Pure-markup authoring
items.desc: A div with data-cf-control + data-cf-id + data-cf-prompt and labelled inputs. The library wires the control and a submit button and styles it from the palette.

items.name: Lock the choice in
items.desc: To reply, read the value and anchor on the control's data-cf-id (a real id in the HTML, unlike runtime cf_ids).

nodes.title: Move 4 — Respond: Reply Inside the Page
nodes.tagline: edit the HTML, then append a batch to history.json

sections.name: The two-part reply
sections.summary: When the Monitor fires, read the full inbox entry for the exact ids, then reply in two parts.

items.name: Part A — edit the HTML
items.desc: Make the change they asked for and wrap the changed region in an anchor: data-cf-change='ch-<slug>'. One anchor per change. Locate the spot by the quote text — anchor.cf_id is assigned at page-load and is NOT in your file.

items.name: Part B — append to history.json
items.desc: Newest last; keep it a valid array. The batch carries comments (echoed back) and changes (id, in_response_to, anchor, title, description). in_response_to must contain the comment id — that clears the 'processing…' banner; anchor must equal a data-cf-change you actually placed.

sections.name: The etiquette
sections.summary: Promptness is the soul of it.

items.name: Answer what's there
items.desc: Even a test comment deserves a real in-doc reply — that IS the proof the loop works.

items.name: Act in the document first, chat second
items.desc: Make the change visible: a green panel, a re-coloured cell.

items.name: When they answer a crux, commit
items.desc: Restyle the chosen option as decided.

nodes.title: Move 0 — The Optional Pre-Step
nodes.tagline: still four moves — this one is numbered 0 because it runs BEFORE Move 1, only when the doc is structured

diagrams.caption: JSON is the source of truth; HTML is a build artifact
diagrams.ascii:
source.json  ──publish.py──►  index.html + one <node>.html per node + left-nav
      ▲                              │
      │                         (never hand-edited)
  you edit here                      │
      │                              ▼
  autorebake.py ◄── on every change ── rebuilds HTML
      │
  publish.py --freeze ──► portable server-free snapshot + .zip

sections.name: Why it's called Move 0
sections.summary: std-doc is FOUR moves: Method, Style, Serve, Respond. This is not a fifth — it's a Move 0: an OPTIONAL pre-step that runs in front of Move 1, and ONLY when a document is structured (many pages over one knowledge base). A single hand-authored page skips it entirely and the four moves are unchanged. It's numbered 0, not 5, precisely because it's additive and comes first — count it if you like, but the method is still four moves.

sections.name: Why a doc-tree
sections.summary: When a document is structured — many pages over one knowledge base — author a canonical source.json and let the HTML be 100% derived. A publisher that renders a complete page from JSON alone proves the JSON had everything; the HTML can't drift because it's regenerated, never edited.

items.name: publish.py
items.desc: Derives HTML from source.json and wires the feedback widget every run (so it can't be stripped by a rewrite).

items.name: autorebake.py
items.desc: Watches source.json and rebuilds the published HTML on every change.

items.name: freeze
items.desc: publish.py --freeze bakes a portable, server-free snapshot plus a .zip. Freezing a diagram doc needs the mermaid CLI — freeze.py refuses rather than ship broken diagrams.

sections.name: The schema
sections.summary: title + nodes[] are required; each node needs slug + title. Everything else is optional. A node becomes one HTML page with sections → items, optional diagrams, badges, and an additive free-form evidence drill-down.

items.name: Additive by design
items.desc: The evidence object is free-form and ignored by any renderer that doesn't opt in — proven by injecting a sample on every node and diffing to a byte-identical render.

items.name: Multi-page note
items.desc: All pages share one feedback/ dir, so when you reply set the change's page field — that's what makes History click-to-navigate across pages.

nodes.title: Lifecycle — When a Doc Earns a Home
nodes.tagline: live ⇄ shelved · locked · sealed — nothing is ever deleted

sections.name: Two orthogonal axes
sections.summary: An ad-hoc doc can live and die with the session. A doc worth keeping gets a durable home: library/<slug>/{index.html, meta.json, feedback/}.

items.name: Liveness (mechanical, reversible)
items.desc: ◉ LIVE (server up) ⇄ ❄ SHELVED (server off, history kept). shelve stops + stamps; wake serves again + re-arms the Monitor.

items.name: Decision (sticky)
items.desc: 🔒 LOCKED = declared final. Seal is the one move to cold storage: strip the injected tags → clean static, then move library/<slug> → archive/<slug>. wake un-archives and restores interactivity.

citations.note: the four verbs: shelve, wake, lock, seal

nodes.title: Gotchas — These Will Bite
nodes.tagline: the unglamorous truths, named out loud

sections.name: Serving
sections.summary: The server is tiny and stdlib-only — which means a few sharp edges.

items.name: --idle-timeout 0 is mandatory
items.desc: The server auto-shuts-down after 600s of no requests by default. A doc you set up before the reader opens it will quietly die in 10 minutes. setup.sh sets it.

items.name: macOS has no setsid
items.desc: Start the server with run_in_background or via setup.sh — never a start that depends on setsid.

items.name: Per-doc nohup dies on parent exit
items.desc: Fine for an ad-hoc doc (dies with your session, by design). For something long-lived, run it under a persistent service.

sections.name: Authoring & files
sections.summary: The traps that have actually cost time.

items.name: inject.py is wiped by full HTML rewrites
items.desc: The widget tags live in the HTML, so regenerating a page from scratch silently strips them. Re-run inject.py after any hand-rewrite. (v2 publish.py re-wires automatically.)

items.name: history.json is append-only
items.desc: Append, never prepend or overwrite — the client walks from the end to find the latest batch.

items.name: Mermaid dark-theme traps
items.desc: Three silent bombs: emoji in subgraph labels, \n in pipe edge labels, Bootstrap classDef colors on a dark theme. Run engine/scripts/mermaid_fix.py and confirm zero bomb icons in a browser.

citations.note: the three silent bombs + fixes + pan-zoom viewer

nodes.title: The Pluggable Renderer — CORE + Primitive Library
nodes.tagline: the moat: add a visual by writing a module, never editing the core

diagrams.caption: the split — CORE owns orchestration, primitives own pixels
diagrams.ascii:
source.json ──► CORE  (walk · numbering · nav · anchors · CSS dedup)
                    │        owns the palette + security gate + freeze
                    │
                    ▼  dispatch each typed block by `type`
               REGISTRY ──► primitive.render(block, ctx) ──► content HTML
                    │             (core wraps the anchor around it)
                    └─ unknown/throwing type ──► visible error block (never crash)

sections.name: Why it exists
sections.summary: A doc engine that documents the kingdom must grow new visuals without a whole-system release. The renderer splits into a stable CORE and a swappable LIBRARY of primitives, so a new component is one self-contained module against a frozen contract.

items.name: The CORE
items.desc: Owns the doc-tree walk, node numbering, left-nav, anchors (data-cf-change / data-cf-anchor), CSS/asset dedup, freeze orchestration, the palette, and the security gate. It never knows what a 'swimlane' is.

citations.note: 7 modules: primitive, registry, blocks, palette, gate, d2, page

items.name: The LIBRARY
items.desc: 13 first-party primitives, each a module under engine/primitives/. Each turns one typed block into HTML and nothing more.

items.name: The moat
items.desc: No other doc engine binds ONE named-entity palette across every component AND closes the agent-edits-back loop. Comment capture is commodity; this pairing is not.

sections.name: How it was built — strangler-fig
sections.summary: The renderer was not rewritten in place. Today's hand-ordered render_node was wrapped as primitives BYTE-IDENTICAL first (the golden-master gate), then the core was hollowed out behind the contract.

items.name: Decisions D1–D6
items.desc: BUILD the renderer + palette (the moat); ADOPT only the diagram layer (D2 binary, Mermaid fallback). Clean-room a ~50-LOC registry (studied markdown-it-py, depend on none). Port the token→CSS pattern (Style Dictionary's idea), stay dependency-free. Contract is language-agnostic so a future Go port re-implements, never re-designs.

items.name: Phased P0–P6
items.desc: P0 contract + probes → P1 strangler-wrap existing renderers → P2 blocks[]+lint → P3 palette + palette-bound primitives → P4 D2 diagrams → P5 security gate → P6 standalone bespoke pages.

citations.note: the by-descent PRD + WBS that drove the build

nodes.title: The Contract — RenderPrimitive
nodes.tagline: seven members, five invariants, one frozen surface

sections.name: The seven members
sections.summary: engine/core/primitive.py defines the one stable contract. render/css/assets/freeze/validate have safe no-op defaults — a text primitive overrides only render (and usually validate).

items.name: type : str
items.desc: The registry key / JSON discriminator. Subclasses MUST set it as a class attribute.

items.name: render(block, ctx) -> html
items.desc: The inner HTML for one block. The core wraps the anchor around your output.

items.name: css() -> str
items.desc: CSS this primitive needs. Collected once and deduped by the core.

items.name: assets() -> [Asset]
items.desc: Declared kit/font deps. The core wires them centrally.

items.name: freeze(block, ctx) -> html | None
items.desc: Zero-external rewrite for a frozen snapshot. None when render() is already external-free (the common case).

items.name: validate(block) -> [error]
items.desc: Schema-fragment lint. Assembled across all installed primitives so the lint can never drift from the renderer.

items.name: needs : {network, kit}
items.desc: What the security gate reads. Default: fully sandboxed (no network, no external kit).

citations.note: contract docstring + RenderPrimitive ABC with no-op defaults

sections.name: The five invariants you must honor
sections.summary: From protocol/primitives.md — the rules a primitive author cannot break.

items.name: 1 · Anchors are core, never yours
items.desc: Emit content only; the core assigns data-cf-anchor. Never write your own data-cf-*.

items.name: 2 · Freeze = zero external refs
items.desc: freeze() output must contain no http(s)://, protocol-relative //host, or CDN src/href. The gate scans it and fails the build naming your type.

items.name: 3 · stdlib only
items.desc: No third-party imports — test_stdlib_only.py enforces it.

items.name: 4 · Helpers arrive via ctx
items.desc: Never import the core. ctx carries esc, palette, registry, anchor, render_evidence, status_class — keeping the contract language-agnostic for the Go port.

items.name: 5 · Be palette-bound where it makes sense
items.desc: ctx['palette'].var(key) returns var(--ent-<key>) and raises loudly on an undeclared entity.

nodes.title: The Registry — Dispatch with a Boundary
nodes.tagline: ~50 LOC, clean-room, stdlib only — and it never lets a page crash

sections.name: Three jobs
sections.summary: A type→handler map plus a dispatch that can never break the page. Studied markdown-it-py's renderer.rules and MJML's component registry; took the shape, wrote our own, depend on neither.

items.name: register(primitive)
items.desc: Install a RenderPrimitive instance under its type.

items.name: lookup(type)
items.desc: Fetch it (None if absent).

items.name: render(type, block, ctx)
items.desc: Dispatch WITH a boundary: an unknown type OR a throwing primitive yields a VISIBLE error block (the Sphinx rule) — never an exception that breaks the page, never a silent drop.

nodes.title: The Palette Engine — One Set of Colors, Every Component
nodes.tagline: ported token→CSS pattern (D3), dependency-free — the moat

diagrams.caption: one declared palette colors everything
diagrams.ascii:
root.palette = { captain:{label,color}, eic:{label,color} }
        │  compile
        ▼
  CSS custom props  --ent-captain  --ent-eic
        │  primitives reference via ctx['palette'].var('captain')
        ▼
  chips · callouts · card-grids · tables · (D2 theme) diagrams  ◄ all one palette

sections.name: How it works
sections.summary: A doc declares one named-entity palette at root. The engine compiles it to CSS custom properties (--ent-<key>) and hands primitives a helper to reference an entity's color.

items.name: Palette.var(key)
items.desc: Returns var(--ent-<key>). One declared set colors chips, callouts, card-grids, tables and (via D2 theme interpolation) diagrams.

items.name: expand_chips(text, palette)
items.desc: Inline entity-chip expansion in prose.

items.name: PaletteError — loud on typo
items.desc: Referencing an undeclared entity is a LOUD error, never a silently colorless component.

nodes.title: The blocks[] Stream + Assembled Lint
nodes.tagline: one typed stream; lint ≡ renderer, by construction

sections.name: How a node becomes blocks
sections.summary: The core walks a typed blocks[] and dispatches each through the registry. Today's friendly node schema (badges / diagrams / children / sections / evidence) is mapped onto that stream by adapt_node — byte-identical to the former hand-ordered render_node.

items.name: adapt_node(node)
items.desc: Maps the friendly schema to blocks in the fixed NODE_BLOCK_ORDER; author-placed body blocks slot between sections and evidence.

items.name: lint ≡ renderer
items.desc: The lint schema is ASSEMBLED from the installed primitives' validate(), so it can never drift from the renderer. An unknown block type is a lint error, mirroring the render-time error boundary.

nodes.title: The Security Gate — Freeze Means Frozen
nodes.tagline: a plugin that sneaks in a CDN can never ship a 'frozen' page

sections.name: Per-primitive freeze enforcement
sections.summary: On --freeze every block's frozen output is scanned for external references. Any leak fails the build LOUDLY, naming the offending primitive type.

items.name: EXTERNAL_REF scan
items.desc: Matches http(s)://, protocol-relative //host, and CDN-ish src=// / href=// / url(https:).

items.name: Reads freeze(), falls back to render()
items.desc: A primitive that cleans itself up on freeze passes even if its live render references the kit. SecurityGateError names the type.

nodes.title: D2 Diagrams + Standalone-Page Mode
nodes.tagline: adopt the diagram binary behind the contract; render bespoke pages through it

sections.name: D2 helper — degrade, never fail
sections.summary: Diagram primitives compile a JSON spec to D2 source and ask this module to render it to SVG. If the d2 binary is absent we DO NOT fail the build.

items.name: have_d2() / render_svg()
items.desc: Availability probe + render. The generated D2 source is binary-independent, so the page still carries the diagram's meaning even when d2 is missing.

items.name: source_block() loud skip
items.desc: Emits a labeled 'diagram source' block plus a loud skip note — mirroring mermaid-cli freeze behavior.

sections.name: Standalone single-page mode
sections.summary: Some artifacts are not doc-tree node pages but one bespoke page (e.g. the hand-authored state-machine.html). A source.json opts in with layout: page + theme + a top-level blocks[].

items.name: render_page() + load_theme()
items.desc: Renders one page from a blocks[] stream through the registry, with a minimal bespoke shell and a named theme stylesheet (themes/<name>.css) shipped inline.

items.name: anchor_attr(block)
items.desc: Primitives read ctx['anchor_attr'](block) to stamp data-cf-change on their own root element — the std-doc anchor convention this page uses.

nodes.title: Write Your Own Plugin — the Whole Contract
nodes.tagline: implement the seven members; drop a module, register one line, ship — no core edit, no release

diagrams.caption: the whole loop

sections.name: Step 1 — the minimum (render only)
sections.summary: A text primitive overrides ONLY render(). css/assets/freeze/validate inherit safe no-op defaults. Extend RenderPrimitive, set type, return content HTML — never an anchor (the core wraps that). Pull helpers from ctx (esc, palette); never import the core.

items.name: class Note(RenderPrimitive)
items.desc:
type='note'; def render(self, block, ctx): return f"
{ctx['esc'](block.get('text',''))}
". That is a complete, shippable primitive.

items.name: Author a block
items.desc: In a node's blocks[]:  { "type": "note", "text": "Heads up." } — it renders where the block asks, nowhere else.

citations.note: the worked note primitive, end to end

sections.name: Step 2 — the full seven members
sections.summary: When your visual needs more than text, here is every member and when to reach for it. All but render() have no-op defaults — implement only what you need.

items.name: type : str
items.desc: The registry key / JSON discriminator. Set it as a class attribute. Required.

items.name: render(block, ctx) -> html
items.desc: Inner HTML for one block. Required. The core wraps the anchor; you emit content only (invariant 1).

items.name: css() -> str
items.desc: Any CSS your component needs. The core collects it ONCE and dedups — return the same string from every instance and it appears in the page <style> a single time.

items.name: assets() -> [Asset]
items.desc: Declared kit scripts / fonts. The core wires them centrally so two primitives needing the same kit don't double-load.

items.name: freeze(block, ctx) -> html | None
items.desc: Zero-external rewrite for a frozen snapshot. Return None when render() is already external-free (text primitives). Diagram primitives override this to inline their SVG (invariant 2).

items.name: validate(block) -> [error]
items.desc: Return human-readable error strings for a malformed block; empty list = valid. The lint ASSEMBLES every installed primitive's validate(), so the schema can never drift from the renderer (invariant 5).

items.name: needs : {network, kit}
items.desc: What the security gate reads. Default fully sandboxed. Declare kit=True only if you genuinely need the browser kit pre-freeze — and freeze() must still inline.

citations.note: the seven members + no-op defaults on the ABC

sections.name: Step 3 — be palette-bound
sections.summary: If your component shows entity colour, bind it to the one declared palette instead of hard-coding hex. This is the moat — one palette colours every component.

items.name: ctx['palette'].var(key)
items.desc: Returns var(--ent-<key>). Use it in your style attribute. Referencing an undeclared entity raises PaletteError loudly — a typo can never silently render colourless (invariant 5).

sections.name: Step 4 — register + test
sections.summary: Two lines and a test file. The golden-master guarantees you broke nothing.

items.name: Register (one line)
items.desc: Add your instance to the register loop in engine/primitives/__init__.py's install(). That's the only place the core learns your type exists.

items.name: Add test_<name>.py
items.desc: One test file per primitive is the convention — pin render() output and validate() rules. Run the suite (~107 tests).

items.name: Golden-master keeps the peace
items.desc: tests/golden + tests/golden_pr hold reference HTML; the strangler proof diffs every existing page byte-for-byte, so a new primitive can never silently change pages that don't use it.

nodes.title: The Test Suite — How We Know It Holds
nodes.tagline: ~107 tests · one per primitive · golden-master byte-identical

sections.name: What's covered
sections.summary: engine/tests/ carries ~107 tests across 22 files — one suite per primitive plus the cross-cutting guarantees that make the architecture trustworthy.

items.name: One test file per primitive
items.desc: test_chip, test_callout, test_cardgrid, test_table, test_swimlane, test_statetrack — each primitive's render + validate is pinned.

items.name: Cross-cutting guarantees
items.desc: test_registry (dispatch + error boundary), test_palette (var + PaletteError), test_lint / test_lint_assembled (lint ≡ renderer), test_security_gate (freeze leak fails loud), test_stdlib_only (no third-party imports), test_strangler (byte-identical wrap), test_page / test_anchors / test_publish / test_search / test_server_port.

items.name: Golden-master suites
items.desc: tests/golden + tests/golden_pr hold reference HTML; the strangler proof diffs new renders against them to guarantee existing pages stay byte-identical.
